subject: Recap & next steps: structured output + function-calling requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finovate.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Recap & next steps: structured output + function-calling requirements

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described:
- Generated responses from your current assistant are too free-form for downstream systems (parsing errors, retry logic).
- Need deterministic outputs for transaction ingestion and compliance reasons.
- Current toolchain: AWS Lambda fronting a webhook, Postgres for transactions, and a simple intermediary agent that runs regex validation.

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Responses that are machine-parseable and either validate against a JSON schema or fail explicitly with a clear error payload.
2) <100ms extra latency introduced by our function-calling layer for 95th percentile requests.
3) End-to-end fewer than 1% downstream ingestion errors for 10k/day production traffic.

Functional requirements we discussed (explicit ask):
- Function-calling support to trigger your payment-processor microservice with a sealed JSON payload.
- Structured-output enforcement via JSON Schema that we can validate server-side; preference for a single canonical schema per intent.
- Agent workflow examples: 1) parse -> validate -> call function; 2) parse -> ask for clarification -> validate -> call function.
- Deterministic formatting: examples and a success definition (e.g., exact key ordering not required, but stable keys and types with no extra nesting).

Attached: security questionnaire stub you asked for (Finovate_Security_Questionnaire_2026.pdf) and a quick CSV of the fields you said were critical (postcall_requirements.csv).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with our platform team to walk through a prototype JSON schema and a sample agent workflow (slots I proposed below).
- We produce a reference schema + 3 example completions (happy path, validation error, clarification prompt) by EOD Friday.
- I'll open a HubSpot record and send a lightweight mutual action plan (MAP).

Suggested times for deep-dive: Thu 2/12 11:00-12:00 PT or Fri 2/13 09:00-10:00 PT. Which works?

Thanks — looking forward to progressing this.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Finovate_Security_Questionnaire_2026.pdf (security questionnaire, 12 pages)
Attachment: postcall_requirements.csv (sample field list)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finovate.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: structured output + function-calling requirements

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- About deterministic formatting: we don't require fixed key ordering, but the output must always include a top-level "transaction" object and a top-level "validation_status" string ("ok" or "error"). If "error", we need an "error_code" and human-friendly "error_message".
- Schema versioning: we want the ability to pin model responses to schema v1/v2 as we iterate. Can Redwood recommend a rollout strategy?
- Latency: the 100ms addition is a target — our internal SLA is currently 200ms p50 for the full stack; anything that keeps overall p95 < 500ms is acceptable for initial pilots.

On process: procurement wants a light statement of our intended flow before we loop them in. I'll share your questionnaire with procurement (procurement@finovate.ai).

Yes to the deep-dive — Thu 2/12 11:00 PT works for the engineering team. Please include a short agenda and the platform engineer(s) who will attend.

One additional ask: can you provide an example of how Redwood would surface deterministic failures (schema mismatch) back to our app, and a recommended retry/backoff pattern? 

Appreciate it — Alex
VP Product, Finovate AI

Subject: Fwd: Recap & next steps: structured output + function-calling requirements

Marissa — forwarding my quick notes after reading Alex's reply. Adding for visibility: Stephanie should join the deep-dive for security/compliance context.

Technical notes / proposed owners:
- Platform deep-dive owners: myself (serving/runtime) and Priya Natarajan (platform integrations) — will prepare a short demo of function-calling + JSON schema enforcement.
- Suggested approach for deterministic errors: standardize an error envelope {"validation_status":"error","error_code":"SCHEMA_MISMATCH","details": {"field":"amount","expected":"number"}} and return with HTTP 422 to signal non-retryable client payload issues.
- Retry/backoff: proactive retries are okay for transient infra errors (HTTP 5xx). For SCHEMA_MISMATCH or other 4xx-style deterministic failures, recommend no automatic retry; instead return structured guidance to the client and surface to logs/alerts.

Action items for our side before Thu:
- Produce a canonical schema example + three sample outputs (happy / validation_error / clarification). Owner: Dylan. Due: EOD Wed 2/11. (I know the date passed; will deliver before the deep-dive.)
- Prepare a short slide showing how we map model call -> function invocation -> downstream webhook with latency numbers and options for prefix caching. Owner: Priya.
- Ensure QA/Canary route for the MAP so we can test pinned schema versions without impacting other traffic.

I'll be on the deep-dive. Thanks.

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
